question: What is the technical difference between Nominal Subtyping (standard inheritance) and Structural Subtyping (typing.Protocol)?

options.text: - Nominal: Types must explicitly inherit from a parent class (class Dog(Animal):).
It allows classes and functions to operate over arbitrary data types while strictly preserving type identity between inputs and outputs.
ParamSpec captures the exact positional and keyword arguments of a callable Callable[P, R], ensuring full type safety through decorators.
It informs type checkers (Mypy, Pyright) that the installed package ships with inline type annotations that should be statically analyzed.

explanation: - Nominal: Types must explicitly inherit from a parent class (class Dog(Animal):). - Structural (Duck Typing): An object matches the type if it possesses the required methods and attributes, without explicit inheritance.
